The following text is from Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel *Jane Eyre*. The narrator, Jane, is an orphan living with her aunt, Mrs. Reed, and Mrs. Reed's three children: Eliza, John, and Georgiana.

The said Eliza, John, and Georgiana were now clustered round their mama in the drawing-room: she lay reclined on a sofa by the fireside, and with her darlings about her (for the time neither quarrelling nor crying) looked perfectly happy. Me, she had dispensed from joining the group; saying, “She regretted to be under the necessity of keeping me at a distance; but that until she heard from Bessie, and could discover by her own observation, that I was endeavouring in good earnest to acquire a more sociable and childlike disposition, a more attractive and sprightly manner—something lighter, franker, more natural, as it were—she really must exclude me from privileges intended only for contented, happy, little children.”
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Mrs. Reed keeps Jane apart from the family group until Jane shows a more cheerful and agreeable manner.
option_b: Jane refuses to join her cousins because they are quarrelling and crying.
option_c: Mrs. Reed asks Bessie to keep Jane company while the rest of the family rests by the fire.
option_d: Jane's cousins invite her to sit with them, but she prefers to be alone.
explanation_en:
Mrs. Reed sits happily with her own children but has “dispensed” Jane from “joining the group.” She says she “must exclude” Jane until she sees that Jane is trying to acquire “a more sociable and childlike disposition.” Choice A states this main idea.

Choice B is wrong because the cousins are “neither quarrelling nor crying,” and it is Mrs. Reed, not Jane, who keeps Jane away. Choice C is wrong because Bessie is mentioned only as someone who will report on Jane's behavior, not as her companion. Choice D is wrong because no one invites Jane; she is excluded.

B noto‘g‘ri: amakivachchalar “na janjallashyapti, na yig‘layapti,” Jeynni esa o‘zi emas, Rid xonim chetda ushlab turibdi. C noto‘g‘ri: Bessi faqat Jeynning xulqi haqida xabar beradigan odam sifatida tilga olinadi, uning hamrohi sifatida emas. D noto‘g‘ri: Jeynni hech kim taklif qilmaydi — u chetlatilgan.

The following text is from Willa Cather's 1913 novel *O Pioneers!* The characters are traveling home from a small town across the Nebraska prairie.

The little town behind them had vanished as if it had never been, had fallen behind the swell of the prairie, and the stern frozen country received them into its bosom. The homesteads were few and far apart; here and there a windmill gaunt against the sky, a sod house crouching in a hollow. But the great fact was the land itself, which seemed to overwhelm the little beginnings of human society that struggled in its sombre wastes. It was from facing this vast hardness that the boy’s mouth had become so bitter; because he felt that men were too weak to make any mark here, that the land wanted to be let alone, to preserve its own fierce strength, its peculiar, savage kind of beauty, its uninterrupted mournfulness.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: The boy is excited about building a farm that will transform the prairie.
option_b: So many homesteads have been built that the prairie is becoming crowded.
option_c: The vast, harsh prairie seems to overwhelm the settlers' small efforts, leaving the boy convinced that people cannot change it.
option_d: The boy thinks that because the prairie is beautiful, it will be easy to farm.
explanation_en:
The text calls the land “the great fact,” says it “seemed to overwhelm the little beginnings of human society,” and explains that the boy felt “men were too weak to make any mark here.” Choice C captures this main idea.

Choice A is wrong because the boy is bitter, not excited, and believes people cannot change the land. Choice B is wrong because the homesteads are “few and far apart.” Choice D is wrong because, although the boy sees a “savage kind of beauty” in the land, he associates it with “fierce strength” and “vast hardness,” not with easy farming.

A noto‘g‘ri: bola hayajonlangan emas, balki tushkun va odamlar bu yerni o‘zgartira olmaydi deb hisoblaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: fermer xo‘jaliklari “kam va bir-biridan uzoqda.” D noto‘g‘ri: bola yerda “yovvoyi go‘zallik”ni ko‘rsa ham, uni “shiddatli kuch” va “ulkan qattiqlik” bilan bog‘laydi, dehqonchilik osonligi bilan emas.

passage: In 2019, volunteers in the town of Chorvoq started a monthly “repair café.” On the first Saturday of each month, people bring broken lamps, radios, bicycles, and clothing to the town library, where volunteers with tools fix them for free. Organizers estimate that the event has already kept hundreds of items out of the town dump. Just as important, they say, visitors are encouraged to watch and help with the repairs, so many now leave knowing how to fix simple problems on their own.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: The town library in Chorvoq has started selling tools to residents.
option_b: Chorvoq's repair café reduces waste and also teaches residents how to make repairs themselves.
option_c: Most of the items brought to Chorvoq's repair café cannot be fixed.
option_d: Volunteers in Chorvoq prefer repairing bicycles to repairing clothing.
explanation_en:
The text describes the repair café's two benefits: it has “kept hundreds of items out of the town dump,” and visitors often “leave knowing how to fix simple problems on their own.” Choice B combines both.

Choice A is wrong because the library hosts the event; nothing suggests it sells tools. Choice C is wrong because the text indicates that many items are repaired and kept out of the dump. Choice D is wrong because the text lists several kinds of items without saying the volunteers prefer any of them.

passage:
The following text is from W. E. B. Du Bois's 1903 book *The Souls of Black Folk*.

After the Egyptian and Indian, the Negro is a sort of seventh son, born with a veil, and gifted with second-sight in this American world,—a world which yields him no true self-consciousness, but only lets him see himself through the revelation of the other world. It is a peculiar sensation, this double-consciousness, this sense of always looking at one’s self through the eyes of others, of measuring one’s soul by the tape of a world that looks on in amused contempt and pity. One ever feels his twoness,—an American, a Negro; two souls, two thoughts, two unreconciled strivings; two warring ideals in one dark body, whose dogged strength alone keeps it from being torn asunder.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Black Americans have fully reconciled their identities as Americans and as people of African descent.
option_b: Most white Americans regard Black Americans with admiration and respect.
option_c: The “second-sight” that Black Americans possess gives them an advantage that outweighs any hardship.
option_d: Being forced to see oneself through the scornful eyes of others leaves Black Americans with a painful sense of being divided between two identities.
explanation_en:
Du Bois describes “double-consciousness” as “always looking at one’s self through the eyes of others,” a world that responds with “amused contempt and pity.” The result is “twoness”: “two unreconciled strivings,” “two warring ideals” that threaten to tear one apart. Choice D captures this main idea.

Choice A is wrong because Du Bois calls the two strivings “unreconciled” and “warring.” Choice B is wrong because the other world looks on with “contempt and pity,” not admiration. Choice C is wrong because, although Du Bois uses the phrase “gifted with second-sight,” he goes on to describe this vision as a source of strain, since it gives “no true self-consciousness”; he never says it outweighs the hardship.
explanation_uz:
Dyu Bua “ikki tomonlama ong”ni (double-consciousness) “o‘zingga doim boshqalarning ko‘zi bilan qarash” deb ta’riflaydi, bu dunyo esa “masxaraomuz nafrat va achinish” bilan qaraydi. Natijada “ikkilik” paydo bo‘ladi: “ikki murosasiz intilish,” insonni parchalab yuborishi mumkin bo‘lgan “ikki kurashuvchi ideal.” D javob shu asosiy g‘oyani ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: Dyu Bua bu ikki intilishni “murosasiz” va “bir-biri bilan kurashuvchi” deb ataydi. B noto‘g‘ri: boshqa dunyo hayrat bilan emas, “nafrat va achinish” bilan qaraydi. C noto‘g‘ri: Dyu Bua “ikkinchi ko‘rish qobiliyati bilan siylangan” iborasini ishlatsa ham, keyin bu ko‘rish “haqiqiy o‘zlikni anglash” bermasligini va og‘ir zo‘riqish manbai ekanini tasvirlaydi; u bu qiyinchilikdan ustun turadi demaydi.

The following text is from Henry David Thoreau's 1862 essay “Walking.”

It is true, we are but faint-hearted crusaders, even the walkers, nowadays, who undertake no persevering, never-ending enterprises. Our expeditions are but tours, and come round again at evening to the old hearth-side from which we set out. Half the walk is but retracing our steps. We should go forth on the shortest walk, perchance, in the spirit of undying adventure, never to return,—prepared to send back our embalmed hearts only as relics to our desolate kingdoms. If you are ready to leave father and mother, and brother and sister, and wife and child and friends, and never see them again,—if you have paid your debts, and made your will, and settled all your affairs, and are a free man; then you are ready for a walk.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Thoreau recommends that walkers plan their routes so that they can return home before evening.
option_b: Thoreau argues that true walking demands a spirit of total adventure and freedom that most walkers of his day lack.
option_c: Thoreau warns that walking is so dangerous that only people without families should attempt it.
option_d: Thoreau describes the history of the crusades and their influence on travel in his time.
explanation_en:
Thoreau complains that modern walkers are “faint-hearted crusaders” whose walks are mere “tours” that return home. He says one should walk “in the spirit of undying adventure,” free of all ties. Choice B states this main idea.

Choice A is wrong because Thoreau criticizes walks that “come round again at evening” to the hearth. Choice C is wrong because it reads Thoreau's exaggeration too literally: he uses the image of leaving family and settling one's affairs to describe the complete freedom and commitment a walker should have, not to warn of physical danger. Choice D is wrong because “crusaders” is a metaphor for walkers; the text does not discuss the history of the crusades.

A noto‘g‘ri: Toro aynan kechqurun o‘choq boshiga qaytadigan sayrlarni tanqid qiladi. passage: Earthquakes are usually detected by seismometers, sensitive instruments that are expensive to install and are often spaced many kilometers apart. Geophysicist Laylo Mirzaeva and her team tested whether the fiber-optic cables that already carry internet data beneath city streets could serve the same purpose. By sending laser pulses through a 20-kilometer cable and measuring tiny changes in the light that bounced back, the team detected several small tremors that the nearest seismometer, 15 kilometers away, had not recorded. Mirzaeva notes that such cables already run beneath most large cities.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Seismometers are no longer needed because fiber-optic cables can detect every earthquake.
option_b: Laser pulses sent through fiber-optic cables can damage internet service during earthquakes.
option_c: Existing fiber-optic cables may offer a widespread and sensitive way to detect earthquakes.
option_d: Small tremors occur more often near large cities than in rural areas.
explanation_en:
Mirzaeva's team used an existing internet cable to detect tremors that a seismometer missed, and she points out that such cables “already run beneath most large cities.” The main idea is that these cables could provide a widespread, sensitive means of detecting earthquakes, as choice C says.

Choice A overstates the findings: one test detected tremors a single distant seismometer missed, which does not show that seismometers are unnecessary or that cables detect every earthquake. Choice B is wrong because the text never mentions damage to internet service. Choice D is wrong because the text does not compare how often tremors occur in different places.
explanation_uz:
Mirzayeva jamoasi mavjud internet kabelidan foydalanib, seysmometr qayd etmagan silkinishlarni aniqlagan. U bunday kabellar “aksariyat yirik shaharlar ostidan allaqachon o‘tganini” ta’kidlaydi. Asosiy g‘oya — bu kabellar zilzilalarni aniqlashning keng tarqalgan va sezgir vositasi bo‘lishi mumkin. To‘g‘ri javob — C.

A natijalarni bo‘rttiradi: bitta sinovda uzoqdagi bitta seysmometr qayd etmagan silkinishlar aniqlangan, bu seysmometrlar keraksiz yoki kabellar har bir zilzilani aniqlaydi degani emas. B noto‘g‘ri: matnda internet xizmatiga zarar haqida gap yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda turli joylarda silkinishlar qanchalik tez-tez bo‘lishi solishtirilmaydi.

passage:
The following text is from Jane Austen's 1813 novel *Pride and Prejudice*. Mr. Bingley has arrived at a ball with his sisters, his brother-in-law Mr. Hurst, and his friend Mr. Darcy.

His brother-in-law, Mr. Hurst, merely looked the gentleman; but his friend Mr. Darcy soon drew the attention of the room by his fine, tall person, handsome features, noble mien, and the report, which was in general circulation within five minutes after his entrance, of his having ten thousand a year. The gentlemen pronounced him to be a fine figure of a man, the ladies declared he was much handsomer than Mr. Bingley, and he was looked at with great admiration for about half the evening, till his manners gave a disgust which turned the tide of his popularity; for he was discovered to be proud, to be above his company, and above being pleased; and not all his large estate in Derbyshire could save him from having a most forbidding, disagreeable countenance, and being unworthy to be compared with his friend.
stem: Which choice best describes how the narrator portrays the guests' judgment of Mr. Darcy?
option_a: As fair and carefully reasoned, since the guests wait until they know Mr. Darcy well before forming an opinion
option_b: As based entirely on his wealth, which the guests continue to admire throughout the evening
option_c: As consistently negative from the moment Mr. Darcy enters the room
option_d: As shifting from admiration to dislike so completely that even the guests' opinion of his looks is reversed
explanation_en:
At first the guests admire Mr. Darcy's “fine, tall person” and “handsome features,” and the ladies find him “much handsomer than Mr. Bingley.” Once his manners make him seem proud, the “tide of his popularity” turns, and suddenly he has “a most forbidding, disagreeable countenance” (face) and is “unworthy to be compared with his friend.” The narrator shows the guests' judgment swinging so far that even their view of his appearance flips, as choice D says.

Choice A is wrong because the guests form opinions within minutes, based on rumor and first impressions. Choice B is wrong because the narrator says that “not all his large estate” could save his reputation, so wealth does not keep their admiration. Choice C is wrong because the guests look at him “with great admiration for about half the evening.”
explanation_uz:
Avvaliga mehmonlar janob Darsining “kelishgan, baland qaddi” va “chiroyli yuz tuzilishi”ga mahliyo bo‘lishadi, xonimlar uni “janob Bingliydan ancha chiroyliroq” deb topishadi. Ammo xulq-atvori uni mag‘rur qilib ko‘rsatgach, “uning shuhrati oqimi teskari burilib ketadi” va birdan u “juda sovuq, yoqimsiz qiyofali” hamda “do‘sti bilan solishtirishga ham arzimaydigan” bo‘lib qoladi. Hikoyachi mehmonlar fikri shu darajada o‘zgarib ketganini, hatto uning tashqi ko‘rinishiga bahosi ham teskarisiga aylanganini ko‘rsatadi. To‘g‘ri javob — D.

A noto‘g‘ri: mehmonlar bir necha daqiqa ichida, mish-mishlar va birinchi taassurot asosida fikr bildirishadi. B noto‘g‘ri: hikoyachi “uning katta mulki ham” obro‘sini saqlab qola olmaganini aytadi, demak boylik hayratni saqlab qolmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: mehmonlar unga “kechaning yarmigacha katta hayrat bilan” qarashgan.

passage: Linguists have often assumed that when two languages are spoken side by side, the language of the more powerful group gradually replaces the other. Studying three centuries of records from a river port where traders speaking two languages lived together, linguist Dilfuza Hamroyeva found a different pattern. Neither language disappeared; instead, each borrowed hundreds of words from the other, and many residents switched between the two depending on whether they were at the market or at home. Hamroyeva cautions, however, that the port may have been unusual, since neither group ever held clear political control over the other.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option_a: Hamroyeva's study of one port suggests that languages in contact do not always replace one another, although conditions at that port may have been unusual.
option_b: Hamroyeva's study proves that languages in contact never replace one another.
option_c: At the river port, the language of the more powerful group gradually replaced the other language.
option_d: Residents of the river port preferred to speak one language at home and avoided it at the market.
explanation_en:
The text contrasts an assumption (the more powerful group's language replaces the other) with Hamroyeva's finding that, at one port, both languages survived and borrowed from each other. It ends with her caution that the port “may have been unusual.” Choice A captures both the finding and its limitation.

Choice B overstates the conclusion: Hamroyeva studied one port and herself warns it may be unusual, so she does not claim replacement “never” happens. Choice C contradicts the text, which says “neither language disappeared.” Choice D distorts a detail: residents switched languages depending on the setting, but the text does not say they avoided either language anywhere, and this detail is not the main idea.
explanation_uz:
Matn bir taxminni (kuchliroq guruhning tili boshqasining o‘rnini egallaydi) Hamroyevaning bir portdagi topilmasi bilan qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi: u yerda ikkala til ham saqlanib qolgan va bir-biridan so‘z olgan. Matn uning port “odatdagidan farqli bo‘lgan bo‘lishi mumkin” degan ehtiyotkor izohi bilan tugaydi. A javob ham topilmani, ham uning cheklovini qamrab oladi.

B xulosani bo‘rttiradi: Hamroyeva faqat bitta portni o‘rgangan va o‘zi u odatiy bo‘lmasligi mumkinligini aytadi, demak u almashinuv “hech qachon” bo‘lmaydi demaydi. C matnga zid: unda “hech bir til yo‘qolmagan” deyilgan. D tafsilotni buzib ko‘rsatadi: aholi vaziyatga qarab tilni almashtirgan, lekin matnda ular biror joyda biror tildan qochgani aytilmagan; bundan tashqari, bu tafsilot asosiy g‘oya emas.
